title: The Selmer clarinet that cracked on the 13th day
summary: Hall tells how his new Selmer cracked in France and was patched in New York and South America.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yes. Yeah, that was in Paris.

And he said, now he got so much order for clarinet that he can't make them all. Okay. He got every country in the world. He just said, come from South America. He said, all the South American country. He said, his factory is working day and night to make clarinet. And it happened. So when I walk in there, the owner's Albert system clarinet he had. He said, I think I have one upstairs. Uh huh. He went and found out and he, and he was very nice too, because he said, I, I told him I never played a Selma before. So he said, I'll give you a break on this. And he gave me a double case and everything. He said, yeah, you made me press the case. A box of wreath and he gave me a cover for the case and everything. Just for me to use the Selma. And I told him, I said, now any chance of this thing cracking? He said, we don't guarantee whether, if you pay a thousand dollars per client, whether it'll crack or not. He said, they usually crack for 10 to 12 days. The 13th day, I pulled it out the, out the case. It was, I think it was the last day it was in France, in the theater. I put it up that night. It was all right, because the next day when I went to the theater, opened my case, the client was cracking. Oh wow. The 13th day, crack. This is on a Saturday night. We leave in Sunday and I can't go back to the factory. The factory's closed. Oh wow. Just lucky enough, I had another client. So I brought the, I brought the client all the way to the United States. When I got to California, the guy wouldn't touch it. There was a fellow on 8th Avenue in New York City. I sent it to him. So he kind of patched it up. And then every other week, I had to change pads on it. So I went down to South America and there's a guy with a saxophone player there and he repaired instruments. And he said, I can fix that client in one leak. So he came to the hotel and made, took about two hours and made two pads for that. I had me in trouble with that client. He says. You have a buffet too. Yeah, I got a buffet too.
